Subject: Question on monthly floor / proration for mixed usage patterns

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency numbers. We have two billing questions from procurement while we finalize the order form:

1) Our app mixes short streaming assistant calls (~100 tokens each) and occasional long-context batch calls (20k tokens) in the same account. How does Redwood apply the monthly minimum / billing floor across those different call types? Are they aggregated into one bucket or treated separately?

2) If we move from pay-as-you-go to a seat bundle mid-billing-cycle (we expect to upgrade on July 7), how do you prorate the floor and any minimums? For example, if the monthly floor is $10k and we commit to a $15k bundle starting mid-month, is there a pro-rated charge, credit, or overlap?

We attached our RFP extract so you can see volume profile. Procurement asked for an example invoice illustrating rounding, proration, and a scenario where streaming + long-context calls cross threshold mid-month.

Appended: Orbital_RFP_pricing.xlsx (sample volumes)

Appreciate a short example and a proposed concession for the first two months if the numbers spike.

Best,
Adam
Head of Finance, Orbital AI

Subject: Re: Question on monthly floor / proration for mixed usage patterns

Hi Adam — great questions. I pulled together the short explainer below and attached our pricing deck with a worked invoice example. TL;DR: we aggregate usage across call types for the floor but meter different unit rates per call shape; proration is pro-rated to the day for new bundles and we can apply a temporary credit for month 1 on a case-by-case basis.

Summary (high level):
- Aggregation: All token usage for the account is summed when evaluating the monthly floor/minimum. We do not create separate floors for streaming vs batch by default.
- Unit rates: Streaming sessions and long-context batch calls can have different per-token prices (we recommend a separate long-context SKU). Those rates are applied to the usage; the floor ensures a minimum invoice total after rate application.
- Proration when upgrading: If you purchase a seat bundle or commit to a minimum mid-cycle, the bundle charge is prorated by days remaining in the billing period. Any pre-existing usage that contributed to the floor still counts. If the new bundle amount exceeds the prorated floor, we bill the higher amount (prorated); if not, we credit the difference back as a line item.

Example (short):
- Month floor: $10,000
- Days in month: 30
- Orbital has used $6,000 in first 7 days (streaming + some batch).
- On day 8 Orbital purchases a $15,000 monthly bundle. Prorated bundle = $15,000 * (23/30) = $11,500. Invoice will show: prorated bundle $11,500, prior usage billed toward floor (we reconcile to ensure you are not double-billed), net due = $11,500 (bundle) and we would issue a credit if previous charges already exceeded the net.

Concession: We can offer a one-time month-1 spike credit up to $4,000 for new contracts moving to a bundle if you can commit to a 6-month minimum. I looped Marcus to confirm.

Attached: redwood-pricing-deck-v3.pdf (worked invoice example)

If you'd like, I can produce a mock invoice for a few permutations from your RFP — happy to walk through on a 30-min call.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Folks — quick internal thread to decide the concession. I reviewed the RFP; Orbital's spike risk looks concentrated in the first 30 days post-launch. Options:

A) Offer 6-month commit + $4k one-time spike credit (Soji suggested)
B) Offer 3-month commit + $2k spike credit + a consumption cap override for month 1 (we absorb overage up to $2k)
C) No credit, but agree to produce two worked invoices and an audit call to walk procurement through rounding/proration.

My take: A is cleanest commercially but might not be necessary for a smaller ARR. I'd prefer B for mid-market — keeps us flexible and protects margin. Vanessa — can you confirm that Finance is OK with a $2k overage buffer for trial month?

Also, we should confirm the product behavior around long-context SKUs: are we comfortable with aggregated-floor logic (I think yes) or do we want to reserve the right to split floors for customers on separate contracts? That affects large accounts.

 —Marcus
Head of Enterprise Sales Ops

Thanks for the context. Finance okayed option B with one tweak: make the $2k overage buffer a rebate (credit) rather than an absorb — that keeps the accounting clean. Conditions:

- Customer must sign a 3-month commit (no refunds).
- We will produce the two worked invoices and include a line item showing how the prorated bundle replaces the floor to avoid confusion for procurement.
- Overage rebate applies only for the first month and is capped at $2,000. We will not extend the rebate for usage caused by clear abuse patterns (excessive streaming test traffic).

Soojin — please send Orbital a short note with the proposed structure and attach the two worked invoice permutations (we should include an explicit example where streaming + 20k batch call pushes them over). Also get a firm yes/no on the 3-month commit from Adam/Saira.
